Patients with rheumatoid arthritis (p.11) taking NSAIDs have shown subjective improvement after 12 months of treatment with evening primrose oil, with or with- out fish oil, when compared with placebo.1 A clinically impor- tant reduction in signs and symptoms of disease activity has also been seen in patients treated with gamolenic acid in the form of borage oil.2 During treatment with evening primrose oil patients with rheumatoid arthritis have increased plasma concentrations of gamolenic, dihomo-gamma-linolenic, and arachidonic acids, and decreased plasma concentrations of oleic and eicosapentaen- oic acids and apolipoprotein B.3 The increase in plasma-arachi- donic acid and decrease in eicosapentaenoic acid might be unfa- vourable in such patients, since arachidonic acid is the precursor of inflammatory prostaglandins and eicosapentaenoic acid may have an anti-inflammatory role. However, a systematic review4 of these and other studies concluded that there does appear to be some potential benefit for the use of gamolenic acid in rheuma- toid arthritis, although optimum dosage and duration of treat- ment remains to be established. 1.
